summary: Typosquat of @whiskeysockets/baileys hijacks integrators' WhatsApp accounts to follow attacker-controlled newsletters
details: @fazzcode/baileys impersonates the legitimate @whiskeysockets/baileys WhatsApp library (matching name pattern, README, and banner). When an integrator calls the main exported makeWASocket() API, the call chain reaches makeNewsletterSocket in lib/Socket/newsletter.js, which schedules a setTimeout for 80 seconds after socket creation. The callback fetches https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tskiofc/channel-id/refs/heads/main/newsletter.json and, for each ID returned, invokes newsletterWMexQuery(id, QueryIds.FOLLOW) — silently subscribing the integrator's authenticated WhatsApp account to channels chosen by an external, attacker-mutable list. The behavior is undocumented and absent from upstream Baileys. The package also declares `libsignal-xeuka: github:tskiofc/libsignal` in package.json with no commit SHA — the same GitHub account (tskiofc) that controls the newsletter target list — giving that actor mutable control over a core cryptography dependency on every install. The attacker benefit is concrete: hijacked WhatsApp identities forced to amplify attacker-chosen channels, plus an unpinned crypto-library supply-chain foothold under the same actor's control.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
